lines.say: Why do your muscles twitch at night?
Why does this happen, number eleven.
That little flicker under your skin is called a fasciculation.
One nerve fires on its own, and a tiny group of muscle fibers twitches. You can't stop it.
It's really common in healthy people. Most notice it at some point.
Hard training makes it more likely. So do caffeine, stress and bad sleep.
In studies following people with harmless twitches for years, they stayed harmless.
But twitching with weakness, or muscles getting smaller? See a doctor.
